{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_3","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md; cat src/fromager/bootstrapper/_start.py'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport typing\n\nfrom ..requirements_file import RequirementType\nfrom ._phase import Phase\nfrom ._prepare_source import PrepareSource\nfrom ._types import BootstrapPhase\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass Start(Phase):\n    \"\"\"Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.\n\n    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the dependency graph, then checks\n    whether this ``(req, version)`` pair has already been processed.  Duplicate\n    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.\n    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack\n    is updated.\n\n    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START\n    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False\n\n    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.\n\n        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),\n        matching the original behavior where graph addition and\n        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.\n\n        Returns:\n            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).\n            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = self.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        assert wi.source_url is not None\n\n        # Add to graph (skip TOP_LEVEL, already added in _resolve_and_add_top_level)\n        if wi.req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:\n            bt.add_to_graph(\n                wi.req,\n                wi.req_type,\n                wi.resolved_version,\n                wi.source_url,\n                wi.parent,\n            )\n\n        wi.build_sdist_only = bt.sdist_only and not wi.is_build_requirement_context()\n\n        if bt.has_been_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only):\n            logger.debug(\n                f\"redundant {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} \"\n                f\"({wi.resolved_version}, sdist_only={wi.build_sdist_only}) \"\n                f\"for {bt.explain}\"\n            )\n            return []\n        bt.mark_as_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only)\n\n        logger.info(\n            f\"new {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} resolves to {wi.resolved_version}\"\n        )\n\n        # Must set pbi_pre_built before constructing PrepareSource so that\n        # PrepareSource.background_work() immediately sees the correct value.\n        pbi = bt.ctx.package_build_info(wi.req)\n        wi.pbi_pre_built = pbi.is_pre_built(wi.resolved_version)\n        wi.exclusive_build = pbi.exclusive_build\n        return [PrepareSource(wi)]\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)


class TestPhaseClassVariables:
    """Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why",
        [
            (Resolve, BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE, False),
            (Start, BootstrapPhase.START, False),
            (PrepareSource, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE, True),
            (PrepareBuild, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD, True),
            (Build, BootstrapPhase.BUILD, True),
            (ProcessInstallDeps, BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS, True),
            (Complete, BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE, True),
        ],
    )

class Cart:
    def __init__(self, tax_rate=0.0):
        self.items = []
        self.tax_rate = tax_rate

    def add(self, price, qty=1):
        self.items.append((price, qty))

    def total(self):
        return compute_total(self.items, self.tax_rate)

def compute_total(items, tax_rate=0.0):
    """Return the total price of items with tax applied.

    items: iterable of (unit_price, quantity)
    """
    subtotal = sum(price * qty for price, qty in items)
    return round(subtotal * (1 + tax_rate), 2)

from app.config import load_config


def test_sections():
    cfg = load_config()
    assert set(cfg) == {"server", "database", "features"}
    assert cfg["server"]["host"] == "0.0.0.0"


def test_values_and_types():
    cfg = load_config()
    assert cfg == {
        "server": {"host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 8080, "debug": False},
        "database": {
            "url": "postgresql://localhost/app",
            "pool_size": 5,
            "timeout": 2.5,
        },
        "features": {"beta": True, "max_upload_mb": 25},
    }
    for section, key in (
        ("server", "port"),
        ("database", "pool_size"),
        ("features", "max_upload_mb"),
    ):
        assert type(cfg[section][key]) is int
    assert type(cfg["database"]["timeout"]) is float
    assert cfg["server"]["debug"] is False
    assert cfg["features"]["beta"] is True


def test_explicit_path(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "custom.toml"
    path.write_text('[server]\nport = 9000\ndebug = true\n', encoding="utf-8")
    assert load_config(path) == {"server": {"port": 9000, "debug": True}}

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence


def distance(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])


def perimeter(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    if len(points) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return sum(distance(points[i], points[(i + 1) % len(points)]) for i in range(len(points)))


def centroid(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    if not points:
        return None
    n = len(points)
    return (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n)


class Polygon:
    def __init__(self, points: Iterable[Sequence[float]], name: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.points = list(points)
        self.name = name

    def area(self) -> float:
        s = 0.0
        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(self.points):
            x2, y2 = self.points[(i + 1) % len(self.points)]
            s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
        return abs(s) / 2

    def scaled(self, factor: float) -> Polygon:
        return Polygon([(x * factor, y * factor) for x, y in self.points], self.name)

    def describe(self) -> dict[str, str | None | int | float]:
        return {"name": self.name, "sides": len(self.points), "area": self.area()}

import time
from collections import OrderedDict


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity, ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.ttl = ttl
        self.clock = clock
        self._entries = OrderedDict()
        self._deadlines = OrderedDict()
        self._stats = dict(hits=0, misses=0, evictions=0, expirations=0)

    def _remove(self, key):
        del self._entries[key]
        self._deadlines.pop(key, None)

    def _expire(self):
        # Fixed TTLs keep deadlines ordered by insertion/update time.
        # Each entry is removed once, giving amortized O(1) cleanup.
        if not self._deadlines:
            return
        now = self.clock()
        while self._deadlines:
            key = next(iter(self._deadlines))
            if self._deadlines[key] > now:
                break
            self._remove(key)
            self._stats["expirations"] += 1

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        self._expire()
        if key not in self._entries:
            self._stats["misses"] += 1
            return default
        self._entries.move_to_end(key)
        self._stats["hits"] += 1
        return self._entries[key]

    def put(self, key, value):
        self._expire()
        self._entries[key] = value
        self._entries.move_to_end(key)
        if self.ttl is not None:
            self._deadlines[key] = self.clock() + self.ttl
            self._deadlines.move_to_end(key)
        if len(self._entries) > self.capacity:
            oldest = next(iter(self._entries))
            self._remove(oldest)
            self._stats["evictions"] += 1

    def delete(self, key):
        self._expire()
        if key not in self._entries:
            return False
        self._remove(key)
        return True

    def stats(self):
        return self._stats.copy()

    def __len__(self):
        self._expire()
        return len(self._entries)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        self._expire()
        return key in self._entries

@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+import unittest
+
+from cachelib.lru import LRUCache
+
+
+class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_invalid_capacity(self):
+        for capacity in (0, -1):
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                LRUCache(capacity)
+
+    def test_get_and_update_change_recency(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
+        cache.put("a", 4)
+        cache.put("d", 5)
+        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 2)
+
+    def test_contains_does_not_change_recency_or_stats(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", None)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        self.assertIn("a", cache)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["hits"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["misses"], 0)
+
+    def test_missing_delete_and_stats_snapshot(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(1)
+        sentinel = object()
+        self.assertIs(cache.get("missing", sentinel), sentinel)
+        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("missing"))
+        cache.put("a", None)
+        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a", sentinel))
+        self.assertTrue(cache.delete("a"))
+        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
+        snapshot = cache.stats()
+        snapshot["hits"] = 99
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=2, evictions=0, expirations=0))
+
+    def test_ttl_boundary_reads_do_not_refresh_and_update_does(self):
+        now = [0]
+        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=5, clock=lambda: now[0])
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        now[0] = 4
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        cache.put("b", 3)
+        now[0] = 5
+        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a"))
+        self.assertIn("b", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 1)
+        now[0] = 9
+        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("b"))
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=1, evictions=0, expirations=2))
+
+    def test_expiration_before_capacity_eviction(self):
+        now = [0]
+        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=2, clock=lambda: now[0])
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        now[0] = 1
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        cache.get("a")
+        now[0] = 2
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+        self.assertIn("b", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)
+        now[0] = 10
+        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 0)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 3)
+
+    def test_zero_ttl_and_no_ttl(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=0, clock=lambda: 0)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)
+        cache = LRUCache(1, clock=lambda: self.fail("clock used without TTL"))
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. import unittest

from cachelib.lru import LRUCache


class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_invalid_capacity(self):
        for capacity in (0, -1):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                LRUCache(capacity)

    def test_get_and_update_change_recency(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        cache.put("c", 3)
        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
        cache.put("a", 4)
        cache.put("d", 5)
        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 4)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 2)

    def test_contains_does_not_change_recency_or_stats(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", None)
        cache.put("b", 2)
        self.assertIn("a", cache)
        cache.put("c", 3)
        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["hits"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["misses"], 0)

    def test_missing_delete_and_stats_snapshot(self):
        cache = LRUCache(1)
        sentinel = object()
        self.assertIs(cache.get("missing", sentinel), sentinel)
        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("missing"))
        cache.put("a", None)
        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a", sentinel))
        self.assertTrue(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
        snapshot = cache.stats()
        snapshot["hits"] = 99
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=2, evictions=0, expirations=0))

    def test_ttl_boundary_reads_do_not_refresh_and_update_does(self):
        now = [0]
        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=5, clock=lambda: now[0])
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)
        now[0] = 4
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        cache.put("b", 3)
        now[0] = 5
        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a"))
        self.assertIn("b", cache)
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 1)
        now[0] = 9
        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("b"))
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=1, evictions=0, expirations=2))

    def test_expiration_before_capacity_eviction(self):
        now = [0]
        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=2, clock=lambda: now[0])
        cache.put("a", 1)
        now[0] = 1
        cache.put("b", 2)
        cache.get("a")
        now[0] = 2
        cache.put("c", 3)
        self.assertIn("b", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)
        now[0] = 10
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 0)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 3)

    def test_zero_ttl_and_no_ttl(self):
        cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=0, clock=lambda: 0)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)
        cache = LRUCache(1, clock=lambda: self.fail("clock used without TTL"))
        cache.put("a", 1)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import argparse
import json
import sys


def count(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    return {"lines": text.count("\n"), "words": len(text.split()), "chars": len(text)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wc")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    total = {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0}
    rc = 0
    files = []
    for path in args.files:
        try:
            c = count(path)
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"wc: {path}: {e.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
            rc = 1
            continue
        if args.json:
            files.append({"path": path, **c})
        else:
            print(f"{c['lines']:>8}{c['words']:>8}{c['chars']:>8} {path}")
        for k in total:
            total[k] += c[k]
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"files": files, "total": total}))
    elif len(args.files) > 1:
        print(f"{total['lines']:>8}{total['words']:>8}{total['chars']:>8} total")
    return rc

+def test_json(tmp_path, capsys):
+    a = tmp_path / "a.txt"
+    b = tmp_path / "b.txt"
+    a.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
+    b.write_text("café")
+    assert main(["--json", str(a), str(b)]) == 0
+    output = capsys.readouterr()
+    assert output.err == ""
+    assert json.loads(output.out) == {
+        "files": [
+            {"path": str(a), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
+            {"path": str(b), "lines": 0, "words": 1, "chars": 4},

+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("json_mode", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_valid_file", [False, True])
+def test_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys, json_mode, has_valid_file):
+    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
+    valid = tmp_path / "valid.txt"
+    valid.write_text("hello\n")
+    paths = [str(missing)]
+    if has_valid_file:
+        paths.append(str(valid))
+    assert main((["--json"] if json_mode else []) + paths) == 1
+    output = capsys.readouterr()
+    assert output.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"
+    if json_mode:
+        counts = {"lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6}
+        assert json.loads(output.out) == {
+            "files": [{"path": str(valid), **counts}] if has_valid_file else [],
+            "total": counts if has_valid_file else {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0},
+        }
+    else:
+        assert output.out == (
+            f"       1       1       6 {valid}\n"
+            "       1       1       6 total\n"
+            if has_valid_file else ""
+        )
+
+

import json

import pytest

from wc.cli import main


def test_text(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main([str(p)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"


def test_json(tmp_path, capsys):
    a = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    b = tmp_path / "b.txt"
    a.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    b.write_text("café")
    assert main(["--json", str(a), str(b)]) == 0
    output = capsys.readouterr()
    assert output.err == ""
    assert json.loads(output.out) == {
        "files": [
            {"path": str(a), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
            {"path": str(b), "lines": 0, "words": 1, "chars": 4},
        ],
        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 4, "chars": 20},
    }


@pytest.mark.parametrize("json_mode", [False, True])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_valid_file", [False, True])
def test_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys, json_mode, has_valid_file):
    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
    valid = tmp_path / "valid.txt"
    valid.write_text("hello\n")
    paths = [str(missing)]
    if has_valid_file:
        paths.append(str(valid))
    assert main((["--json"] if json_mode else []) + paths) == 1
    output = capsys.readouterr()
    assert output.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"
    if json_mode:
        counts = {"lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6}
        assert json.loads(output.out) == {
            "files": [{"path": str(valid), **counts}] if has_valid_file else [],
            "total": counts if has_valid_file else {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0},
        }
    else:
        assert output.out == (
            f"       1       1       6 {valid}\n"
            "       1       1       6 total\n"
            if has_valid_file else ""
        )


def test_text_multiple_files(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main([str(p), str(p)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == (
        f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"
        f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"
        "       4       6      32 total\n"
    )

"""Parse access logs and aggregate their request statistics."""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from math import ceil, isfinite
from typing import Iterable


@dataclass
class Record:
    ts: datetime
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    latency_ms: float
    bytes: int


@dataclass
class Summary:
    total: int
    malformed: int
    by_status: dict[int, int]
    by_method: dict[str, int]
    p50_latency_ms: float
    p95_latency_ms: float
    bytes_total: int
    error_rate: float
    top_paths: list[tuple[str, int]]


def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
    """Return a parsed record, or None when a line has invalid fields."""
    fields = line.split()
    if len(fields) not in (5, 6):
        return None
    timestamp, method, path, status_text, latency_text = fields[:5]
    try:
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
            return None
        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        status = int(status_text)
        latency = float(latency_text)
        byte_count = int(fields[5]) if len(fields) == 6 else 0
    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
        return None
    if not isfinite(latency):
        return None
    return Record(ts, method, path, status, latency, byte_count)


def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
    """Aggregate valid records and count every malformed input line."""
    statuses: Counter[int] = Counter()
    methods: Counter[str] = Counter()
    paths: Counter[str] = Counter()
    latencies: list[float] = []
    malformed = bytes_total = errors = 0
    for line in lines:
        record = parse_line(line)
        if record is None:
            malformed += 1
            continue
        statuses[record.status] += 1
        methods[record.method] += 1
        paths[record.path] += 1
        latencies.append(record.latency_ms)
        bytes_total += record.bytes
        errors += record.status >= 500
    latencies.sort()
    total = len(latencies)
    return Summary(
        total=total,
        malformed=malformed,
        by_status=dict(statuses),
        by_method=dict(methods),
        p50_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.50) - 1] if total else 0.0,
        p95_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.95) - 1] if total else 0.0,
        bytes_total=bytes_total,
        error_rate=errors / total if total else 0.0,
        top_paths=sorted(paths.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
    )

+def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
+    """Return a parsed record, or None when a line has invalid fields."""
+    fields = line.split()
+    if len(fields) not in (5, 6):
+        return None
+    timestamp, method, path, status_text, latency_text = fields[:5]
+    try:
+        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
+            return None
+        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)
+        status = int(status_text)
+        latency = float(latency_text)
+        byte_count = int(fields[5]) if len(fields) == 6 else 0
+    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
+        return None
+    if not isfinite(latency):
+        return None
+    return Record(ts, method, path, status, latency, byte_count)
+
+
+def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
+    """Aggregate valid records and count every malformed input line."""
+    statuses: Counter[int] = Counter()
+    methods: Counter[str] = Counter()
+    paths: Counter[str] = Counter()
+    latencies: list[float] = []
+    malformed = bytes_total = errors = 0
+    for line in lines:
+        record = parse_line(line)
+        if record is None:
+            malformed += 1
+            continue
+        statuses[record.status] += 1
+        methods[record.method] += 1
+        paths[record.path] += 1
+        latencies.append(record.latency_ms)
+        bytes_total += record.bytes
+        errors += record.status >= 500
+    latencies.sort()
+    total = len(latencies)
+    return Summary(
+        total=total,
+        malformed=malformed,
+        by_status=dict(statuses),
+        by_method=dict(methods),
+        p50_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.50) - 1] if total else 0.0,
+        p95_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.95) - 1] if total else 0.0,
+        bytes_total=bytes_total,
+        error_rate=errors / total if total else 0.0,
+        top_paths=sorted(paths.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
+    )

+++ b/tests/test_parse.py
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from logstats.parse import parse_line, summarize
+
+
+def test_parse_optional_bytes_and_normalize_timezone():
+    record = parse_line("2026-10-01T14:00:00+02:00 GET /health 200 0.4")
+    assert record is not None
+    assert record.ts == datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    assert record.bytes == 0
+    assert record.latency_ms == 0.4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line", [
+    "", "garbage line here",
+    "invalid GET / 200 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET / 200 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / bad 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 bad",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 nan",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 bad",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 2 extra",
+])
+def test_malformed_lines(line):
+    assert parse_line(line) is None
+
+
+def test_sample_summary():
+    with (Path(__file__).parents[1] / "sample.log").open() as lines:
+        result = summarize(lines)
+    assert result.total == 5
+    assert result.malformed == 1
+    assert result.by_status == {200: 2, 201: 1, 404: 1, 500: 1}
+    assert result.by_method == {"GET": 4, "POST": 1}
+    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 12.5
+    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 120.0
+    assert result.bytes_total == 963
+    assert result.error_rate == 0.2
+    assert result.top_paths == [("/api/users", 3), ("/api/users/7", 1), ("/health", 1)]
+
+
+def test_empty_summary():
+    result = summarize(iter(["bad"]))
+    assert result.total == 0
+    assert result.malformed == 1
+    assert result.p50_latency_ms == result.p95_latency_ms == 0.0
+    assert result.error_rate == 0.0
+    assert result.bytes_total == 0
+    assert result.by_status == result.by_method == {}
+    assert result.top_paths == []
+
+
+def test_nearest_rank_and_top_five_tie_order():
+    result = summarize(
+        f"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /{index:02} 503 {index} 2"
+        for index in range(20, 0, -1)
+    )
+    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 10
+    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 19
+    assert result.top_paths == [(f"/{index:02}", 1) for index in range(1, 6)]
+    assert result.error_rate == 1.0
+    assert result.bytes_total == 40

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from logstats.parse import parse_line, summarize


def test_parse_optional_bytes_and_normalize_timezone():
    record = parse_line("2026-10-01T14:00:00+02:00 GET /health 200 0.4")
    assert record is not None
    assert record.ts == datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert record.bytes == 0
    assert record.latency_ms == 0.4


@pytest.mark.parametrize("line", [
    "", "garbage line here",
    "invalid GET / 200 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET / 200 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / bad 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 bad",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 nan",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 bad",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 2 extra",
])
def test_malformed_lines(line):
    assert parse_line(line) is None


def test_sample_summary():
    with (Path(__file__).parents[1] / "sample.log").open() as lines:
        result = summarize(lines)
    assert result.total == 5
    assert result.malformed == 1
    assert result.by_status == {200: 2, 201: 1, 404: 1, 500: 1}
    assert result.by_method == {"GET": 4, "POST": 1}
    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 12.5
    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 120.0
    assert result.bytes_total == 963
    assert result.error_rate == 0.2
    assert result.top_paths == [("/api/users", 3), ("/api/users/7", 1), ("/health", 1)]


def test_empty_summary():
    result = summarize(iter(["bad"]))
    assert result.total == 0
    assert result.malformed == 1
    assert result.p50_latency_ms == result.p95_latency_ms == 0.0
    assert result.error_rate == 0.0
    assert result.bytes_total == 0
    assert result.by_status == result.by_method == {}
    assert result.top_paths == []


def test_nearest_rank_and_top_five_tie_order():
    result = summarize(
        f"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /{index:02} 503 {index} 2"
        for index in range(20, 0, -1)
    )
    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 10
    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 19
    assert result.top_paths == [(f"/{index:02}", 1) for index in range(1, 6)]
    assert result.error_rate == 1.0
    assert result.bytes_total == 40

+def test_default_tags_are_independent():
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
+    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
+    warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags.append("metal")
+    assert warehouse.stock["nut"].tags == []
+
+
+def test_explicit_containers_are_preserved():
+    stock = {}
+    history = []
+    tags = ["metal"]
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a", stock, history)
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, tags)
+    assert warehouse.stock is stock
+    assert warehouse.history is history
+    assert stock["bolt"].tags is tags
+    assert history == [("restock", "bolt", 5)]
+
+
+def test_restock_and_ship():
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
+    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 3)
+    warehouse.ship("bolt", 4)
+    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
+    assert list(warehouse.report()) == ["bolt", "nut"]
+    assert warehouse.history[-1] == ("ship", "bolt", 4)
+    history = warehouse.history.copy()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="insufficient stock"):
+        warehouse.ship("bolt", 5)
+    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
+    assert warehouse.history == history

import pytest

from inv.warehouse import Warehouse


def test_independent_warehouses():
    a = Warehouse("a")
    a.restock("bolt", 5)
    b = Warehouse("b")
    assert b.report() == {}
    b.restock("nut", 2)
    assert a.report() == {"bolt": 5}
    assert len(b.history) == 1


def test_default_tags_are_independent():
    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
    warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags.append("metal")
    assert warehouse.stock["nut"].tags == []


def test_explicit_containers_are_preserved():
    stock = {}
    history = []
    tags = ["metal"]
    warehouse = Warehouse("a", stock, history)
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, tags)
    assert warehouse.stock is stock
    assert warehouse.history is history
    assert stock["bolt"].tags is tags
    assert history == [("restock", "bolt", 5)]


def test_restock_and_ship():
    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 3)
    warehouse.ship("bolt", 4)
    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
    assert list(warehouse.report()) == ["bolt", "nut"]
    assert warehouse.history[-1] == ("ship", "bolt", 4)
    history = warehouse.history.copy()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="insufficient stock"):
        warehouse.ship("bolt", 5)
    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
    assert warehouse.history == history

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int = 0
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)


class Warehouse:
    def __init__(self, name, stock=None, history=None):
        self.name = name
        self.stock = {} if stock is None else stock
        self.history = [] if history is None else history

    def restock(self, sku, qty, tags=None):
        item = self.stock.get(sku)
        if item is None:
            item = Item(sku, 0, [] if tags is None else tags)
            self.stock[sku] = item
        item.qty += qty
        self.history.append(("restock", sku, qty))

    def ship(self, sku, qty):
        item = self.stock[sku]
        if item.qty < qty:
            raise ValueError("insufficient stock")
        item.qty -= qty
        self.history.append(("ship", sku, qty))

    def report(self):
        return {sku: item.qty for sku, item in sorted(self.stock.items())}

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def next_run(now: datetime, hour: int, minute: int, tz: str) -> datetime:
    """Next hour:minute in tz strictly after now. `now` may be naive (treated as UTC) or aware."""
    if now.tzinfo is None:
        now = now.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz)
    today = now.astimezone(zone).date()
    candidate = datetime(today.year, today.month, today.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    if candidate <= now:
        tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
        candidate = datetime(tomorrow.year, tomorrow.month, tomorrow.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    return candidate

+    now = datetime(2026, month, day, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    nxt = next_run(now, 9, 15, "Europe/Berlin")
+    assert nxt == datetime(2026, month, next_day, 9, 15, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
+    assert nxt.utcoffset().total_seconds() == offset * 3600
+    assert nxt > now

Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. from datetime import datetime, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest

from sched import next_run


def test_result_is_after_now_late_evening_utc():
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 23, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)   # already 01:30 on June 2 in Berlin
    nxt = next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin")
    assert nxt > now
    assert (nxt.year, nxt.month, nxt.day, nxt.hour) == (2026, 6, 3, 1)


def test_uses_local_date_before_scheduled_time():
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 22, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin") == datetime(
        2026, 6, 2, 1, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("month, day, next_day, offset", [(3, 28, 29, 2), (10, 24, 25, 1)])
def test_preserves_wall_clock_time_across_dst(month, day, next_day, offset):
    now = datetime(2026, month, day, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    nxt = next_run(now, 9, 15, "Europe/Berlin")
    assert nxt == datetime(2026, month, next_day, 9, 15, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
    assert nxt.utcoffset().total_seconds() == offset * 3600
    assert nxt > now


@pytest.mark.parametrize("aware", [False, True])
def test_exact_match_advances_to_next_day(aware):
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 7, tzinfo=timezone.utc if aware else None)
    assert next_run(now, 9, 0, "Europe/Berlin") == datetime(
        2026, 6, 2, 9, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    )

import threading
import time


class Counter:
    """Named counters. Intended to be shared across request-handler threads."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._values = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def incr(self, name, by=1):
        with self._lock:
            current = self._values.get(name, 0)
            time.sleep(0)  # yield, simulates real work between read and write
            self._values[name] = current + by

    def get(self, name):
        with self._lock:
            return self._values.get(name, 0)

    def snapshot(self):
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._values)

    def reset(self, name=None):
        with self._lock:
            if name is None:
                self._values.clear()
            else:
                self._values.pop(name, None)

+def test_snapshot_is_an_independent_plain_dict():
+    c = Counter()
+    assert c.get("missing") == 0
+    c.incr("hits", by=3)
+    snapshot = c.snapshot()
+    assert type(snapshot) is dict
+    assert snapshot == {"hits": 3}
+    c.incr("hits")
+    c.reset("missing")
+    c.reset("hits")

+    snapshot["other"] = 10
+    assert c.snapshot() == {}
+    c.incr("hits")
+    c.reset()
+    assert c.snapshot() == {}
+

+def test_snapshot_during_updates():
+    c = Counter()
+    done = threading.Event()
+
+    def work():
+        try:
+            for i in range(1000):
+                c.incr(str(i))
+        finally:
+            done.set()
+
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=work)
+    thread.start()
+    try:
+        while not done.is_set():
+            snapshot = c.snapshot()
+            assert type(snapshot) is dict
+            assert snapshot == {str(i): 1 for i in range(len(snapshot))}
+    finally:
+        thread.join()
+    assert len(c.snapshot()) == 1000
+
+
+def test_counter_instances_have_independent_locks():
+    first = Counter()
+    second = Counter()
+    done = threading.Event()
+
+    def work():
+        second.incr("hits")
+        done.set()
+
+    with first._lock:
+        thread = threading.Thread(target=work)
+        thread.start()
+        completed = done.wait(timeout=2)
+    thread.join()
+    assert completed
+    assert second.get("hits") == 1

import threading

from metrics import Counter


def test_no_lost_updates():
    c = Counter()

    def work():
        for _ in range(2000):
            c.incr("hits")

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(8)]
    [t.start() for t in ts]; [t.join() for t in ts]
    assert c.get("hits") == 16000


def test_snapshot_is_an_independent_plain_dict():
    c = Counter()
    assert c.get("missing") == 0
    c.incr("hits", by=3)
    snapshot = c.snapshot()
    assert type(snapshot) is dict
    assert snapshot == {"hits": 3}
    c.incr("hits")
    c.reset("missing")
    c.reset("hits")
    assert snapshot == {"hits": 3}
    snapshot["other"] = 10
    assert c.snapshot() == {}
    c.incr("hits")
    c.reset()
    assert c.snapshot() == {}


def test_snapshot_during_updates():
    c = Counter()
    done = threading.Event()

    def work():
        try:
            for i in range(1000):
                c.incr(str(i))
        finally:
            done.set()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=work)
    thread.start()
    try:
        while not done.is_set():
            snapshot = c.snapshot()
            assert type(snapshot) is dict
            assert snapshot == {str(i): 1 for i in range(len(snapshot))}
    finally:
        thread.join()
    assert len(c.snapshot()) == 1000


def test_counter_instances_have_independent_locks():
    first = Counter()
    second = Counter()
    done = threading.Event()

    def work():
        second.incr("hits")
        done.set()

    with first._lock:
        thread = threading.Thread(target=work)
        thread.start()
        completed = done.wait(timeout=2)
    thread.join()
    assert completed
    assert second.get("hits") == 1

from .registry import UnknownFormat, get


def _extension(fmt):
    return get(fmt).extension


def export_records(records, fmt):
    """records: list of dicts with identical keys. Returns bytes."""
    return get(fmt).dump(records)


def export_to_file(records, fmt, path):
    exporter = get(fmt)
    path = str(path)
    if not path.endswith(exporter.extension):
        path += exporter.extension
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(exporter.dump(records))
    return path

import csv
import io

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class CSVExporter(Exporter):
    name = "csv"
    extension = ".csv"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        buf = io.StringIO()
        if records:
            w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=list(records[0].keys()), lineterminator="\n")
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(records)
        return buf.getvalue().encode()

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class UnknownFormat(ValueError):
    pass


class Exporter(ABC):
    name: str
    extension: str

    @abstractmethod
    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        """Serialize records to bytes."""


_exporters = {}


def register(exporter_cls):
    """Register an exporter class and return it for decorator use."""
    _exporters[exporter_cls.name] = exporter_cls
    return exporter_cls


def names():
    """Return the registered format names in sorted order."""
    return sorted(_exporters)


def get(name):
    """Return a new exporter instance for a registered format."""
    try:
        exporter_cls = _exporters[name]
    except KeyError:
        raise UnknownFormat(
            f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {', '.join(names())}"
        ) from None
    return exporter_cls()

+from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
+
+from ..registry import Exporter, register
+
+
+@register
+class XMLExporter(Exporter):
+    name = "xml"
+    extension = ".xml"
+
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        parts = ["<records>"]
+        for r in records:
+            parts.append("  <record>")
+            for k, v in r.items():
+                parts.append(f"    <{k}>{escape(str(v))}</{k}>")
+            parts.append("  </record>")
+        parts.append("</records>")
+        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

+
+

+class Exporter(ABC):
+    name: str
+    extension: str
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        """Serialize records to bytes."""
+
+
+_exporters = {}
+
+
+def register(exporter_cls):
+    """Register an exporter class and return it for decorator use."""
+    _exporters[exporter_cls.name] = exporter_cls
+    return exporter_cls
+
+
+def names():
+    """Return the registered format names in sorted order."""
+    return sorted(_exporters)
+
+
+def get(name):
+    """Return a new exporter instance for a registered format."""
+    try:
+        exporter_cls = _exporters[name]
+    except KeyError:
+        raise UnknownFormat(
+            f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {', '.join(names())}"
+        ) from None

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from export import Exporter, get, names, register, export_records, export_to_file, UnknownFormat
from export import registry

R = [{"id": 1, "name": "a&b"}, {"id": 2, "name": "c"}]


def test_csv():
    assert export_records(R, "csv") == b"id,name\n1,a&b\n2,c\n"


def test_json():
    assert json.loads(export_records(R, "json")) == R


def test_xml():
    assert b"<name>a&amp;b</name>" in export_records(R, "xml")


def test_file_extension(tmp_path):
    p = export_to_file(R, "json", tmp_path / "out")
    assert p.endswith(".json")


def test_unknown():
    try:
        export_records(R, "yaml")
    except UnknownFormat:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError


def test_builtin_registry():
    assert names() == ["csv", "json", "xml"]
    for name in names():
        exporter = get(name)
        assert isinstance(exporter, Exporter)
        assert exporter.name == name
        assert exporter.extension == "." + name


def test_custom_plugin(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_exporters", registry._exporters.copy())

    @register
    class TextExporter(Exporter):
        name = "text"
        extension = ".txt"

        def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
            return str(len(records)).encode()

    assert isinstance(get("text"), TextExporter)
    assert "text" in names()
    assert export_records(R, "text") == b"2"
    path = export_to_file(R, "text", tmp_path / "out")
    assert path == str(tmp_path / "out.txt")
    assert Path(path).read_bytes() == b"2"
    assert export_to_file(R, "text", path) == path


@pytest.mark.parametrize("operation", [get, lambda fmt: export_records(R, fmt)])
def test_unknown_lists_formats(operation):
    with pytest.raises(UnknownFormat) as error:
        operation("missing")
    assert "missing" in str(error.value)
    assert "csv, json, xml" in str(error.value)


def test_unknown_file_does_not_write(tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(UnknownFormat, match="csv, json, xml"):
        export_to_file(R, "missing", tmp_path / "out")
    assert list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("fmt, expected", [
    ("csv", b""), ("json", b"[]\n"), ("xml", b"<records>\n</records>\n"),
])
def test_empty_records(fmt, expected):
    assert export_records([], fmt) == expected

from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class XMLExporter(Exporter):
    name = "xml"
    extension = ".xml"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        parts = ["<records>"]
        for r in records:
            parts.append("  <record>")
            for k, v in r.items():
                parts.append(f"    <{k}>{escape(str(v))}</{k}>")
            parts.append("  </record>")
        parts.append("</records>")
        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

The default transport uses `asyncio.sleep` to simulate latency\n  as the sync one uses `time.sleep`.\n- `get_many` runs requests concurrently with a concurrency limit `max_concurrency`\n  (constructor arg, default 5).   \ runs the\n  async code with `asyncio.run` for callers that are not async.\n\nPort the existing tests to pytest-asyncio or plain `asyncio.run`, keep them passing, and\nrun them.\n"

from .client import FetchError


async def summarize(client, urls):
    results = await client.get_many(urls)
    ok = [r for r in results if not isinstance(r, FetchError)]
    failed = [r.url for r in results if isinstance(r, FetchError)]
    return {"ok": len(ok), "failed": failed, "bytes": sum(len(r) for r in ok)}

import asyncio


class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, url, cause):
        super().__init__(f"{url}: {cause}")
        self.url = url
        self.cause = cause


class TransientError(Exception):
    pass


async def default_transport(url):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    if url.endswith("/404"):
        raise KeyError("not found")
    return f"payload for {url}".encode()


class Client:
    def __init__(self, transport=None, retries=3, backoff=0.01, max_concurrency=5):
        if max_concurrency < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_concurrency must be at least 1")
        self.transport = transport or default_transport
        self.retries = retries
        self.backoff = backoff
        self.closed = False
        self.calls = 0
        self.max_concurrency = max_concurrency
        self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)

    async def get(self, url):
        if self.closed:
            raise RuntimeError("client closed")
        delay = self.backoff
        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
            self.calls += 1
            try:
                return await self.transport(url)
            except TransientError:
                if attempt == self.retries:
                    raise
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay *= 2

    async def get_many(self, urls):
        async def fetch(url):
            async with self._semaphore:
                try:
                    return await self.get(url)
                except Exception as exc:
                    return FetchError(url, exc)

        return await asyncio.gather(*(fetch(url) for url in urls))

    async def close(self):
        self.closed = True

    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        await self.close()

import asyncio

from .client import Client


def fetch_all(urls, transport=None):
    async def fetch():
        async with Client(transport) as client:
            return await client.get_many(urls)

    return asyncio.run(fetch())

import asyncio

import pytest

from fetcher import Client, FetchError, TransientError, aggregate
from fetcher.sync import fetch_all


def test_get_and_many():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as c:
            assert await c.get("http://x/1") == b"payload for http://x/1"
            res = await c.get_many(["http://x/1", "http://x/404"])
            assert res[0].startswith(b"payload")
            assert isinstance(res[1], FetchError)
            assert res[1].url == "http://x/404"
            assert isinstance(res[1].cause, KeyError)
        assert c.closed
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="client closed"):
            await c.get("u")

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_retry_then_succeed(monkeypatch):
    attempts = {"n": 0}
    delays = []

    async def sleep(delay):
        delays.append(delay)

    async def flaky(url):
        attempts["n"] += 1
        if attempts["n"] < 3:
            raise TransientError("try again")
        return b"ok"

    monkeypatch.setattr("fetcher.client.asyncio.sleep", sleep)

    async def run():
        c = Client(transport=flaky, retries=3)
        assert await c.get("u") == b"ok" and c.calls == 3

    asyncio.run(run())
    assert delays == [0.01, 0.02]


def test_summarize():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as c:
            assert await aggregate.summarize(c, ["http://x/1", "http://x/404"]) == {
                "ok": 1, "failed": ["http://x/404"],
                "bytes": len(b"payload for http://x/1")}

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_concurrency_and_order():
    async def run():
        active = 0
        peak = 0
        started = asyncio.Event()
        release = asyncio.Event()

        async def transport(url):
            nonlocal active, peak
            active += 1
            peak = max(peak, active)
            if active == 2:
                started.set()
            try:
                await release.wait()
                return url.encode()
            finally:
                active -= 1

        async with Client(transport, max_concurrency=2) as client:
            task = asyncio.create_task(client.get_many(["a", "b", "c", "d"]))
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(started.wait(), timeout=1)
            finally:
                release.set()
            assert await task == [b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d"]
            assert peak == 2
            assert await client.get_many([]) == []

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_errors_and_retry_exhaustion():
    async def run():
        attempts = {}

        async def transport(url):
            attempts[url] = attempts.get(url, 0) + 1
            if url == "transient":
                raise TransientError("retry")
            if url == "permanent":
                raise ValueError("fail")
            return b"ok"

        async with Client(transport, retries=3, backoff=0) as c:
            result = await c.get_many(["transient", "permanent", "ok"])
            assert isinstance(result[0].cause, TransientError)
            assert isinstance(result[1].cause, ValueError)
            assert result[2] == b"ok"
            assert attempts == {"transient": 3, "permanent": 1, "ok": 1}
            assert c.calls == 5
            with pytest.raises(TransientError):
                await c.get("transient")

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_sync_wrapper():
    async def transport(url):
        if url == "bad":
            raise ValueError("fail")
        return url.encode()

    result = fetch_all(["a", "bad"], transport)
    assert result[0] == b"a"
    assert isinstance(result[1], FetchError)
    assert fetch_all(["http://x/1"]) == [b"payload for http://x/1"]


def test_invalid_concurrency():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_concurrency"):
        Client(max_concurrency=0)

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule


def test_simple_total():
    inv = build_invoice("A1", [("x", "10.00", 2), ("y", "0.50", 1)])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("20.50")
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("20.50")


def test_with_tax():
    inv = build_invoice("A2", [("x", "100.00", 1)], TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")))
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("119.00")


def test_discount_whole_numbers():
    inv = build_invoice("A3", [("x", "100.00", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10"))])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("90.00")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "tax_rule, expected",
    [(None, Decimal("0.10")), (TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")), Decimal("0.12"))],
)
def test_discount_total_uses_rounded_line_amounts(tax_rule, expected):
    discount = percent_off("TEN", "10")
    inv = build_invoice(
        "A4",
        [("x", "0.05", 1, discount), ("y", "0.05", 1, discount)],
        tax_rule,
    )
    assert line_totals(inv) == [Decimal("0.05"), Decimal("0.05")]
    assert invoice_total(inv) == expected

"""Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total()."""
from decimal import Decimal

from .discounts import apply_discount
from .invoice import Invoice
from .money import round_money
from .tax import tax_for


def line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line."""
    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]


def invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:
    """Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum."""
    net = sum(line_totals(inv), Decimal("0.00"))
    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))

import re
import unicodedata

_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def email_key(email):
    return email.strip().casefold()


def name_key(name):
    """Key for matching names: case-folded, single spaces, no accents."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", name.casefold())
    s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.category(c).startswith("M"))
    return _WS.sub(" ", s.strip())


def dedupe(records):
    """records: list of dicts with 'name' and 'email'. Returns survivors in first-seen order."""
    seen_names, seen_emails, out, parents = {}, {}, [], []

    def root(index):
        while parents[index] != index:
            parents[index] = parents[parents[index]]
            index = parents[index]
        return index

    for r in records:
        index = len(out)
        out.append(r)
        parents.append(index)
        nk, ek = name_key(r["name"]), email_key(r["email"])
        for key, seen in ((nk, seen_names), (ek, seen_emails)):
            if key in seen:
                first, second = root(index), root(seen[key])
                # Keep the earliest record even when a later record bridges groups.
                parents[max(first, second)] = min(first, second)
            else:
                seen[key] = index
    return [r for index, r in enumerate(out) if root(index) == index]

+import unittest
+
+from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve
+
+
+class ResolverTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_versions(self):
+        self.assertEqual(Version('1'), Version('1.0.0'))
+        self.assertEqual(hash(Version('1')), hash(Version('1.0')))
+        self.assertGreater(Version('1.10'), Version('1.9'))
+        self.assertLess(Version('1.0'), Version('1.0.1'))
+        self.assertEqual(str(Version('01.0')), '01.0')
+
+    def test_constraints(self):
+        constraint = Constraint.parse('json>=2,<3,!=2.5')
+        self.assertEqual(constraint.name, 'json')
+        for raw, allowed in [('2', True), ('2.5', False), ('3', False), ('1', False)]:
+            self.assertEqual(constraint.allows(Version(raw)), allowed)
+        for op, allowed in [('==', True), ('!=', False), ('<', False),
+                            ('<=', True), ('>', False), ('>=', True)]:
+            self.assertEqual(Constraint.parse('x' + op + '1').allows(Version('1.0')), allowed)
+        self.assertTrue(Constraint.parse('x').allows(Version('0')))
+
+    def test_backtracking(self):
+        index = {'app': {'1.0': ['web>=2', 'db']},
+                 'web': {'2.0': ['json<3'], '2.1': ['json>=3']},
+                 'json': {'2.0': [], '3.0': []}, 'db': {'1.0': ['json<3']},
+                 'unused': {'9': []}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(['app'], index),
+                         {'app': '1.0', 'db': '1.0', 'json': '2.0', 'web': '2.0'})
+
+    def test_global_preference(self):
+        index = {'z': {'2': ['a==1'], '1': ['a==2']}, 'a': {'1': [], '2': []}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(['z'], index), {'a': '2', 'z': '1'})
+
+    def test_cycles_and_late_constraint(self):
+        index = {'a': {'2': ['b'], '1': ['b']}, 'b': {'1': ['a<2']}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(['a'], index), {'a': '1', 'b': '1'})
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(['a'], {'a': {'1': ['a==1']}}), {'a': '1'})
+

"""Resolve dotted-integer package versions with propagated constraints."""

from functools import total_ordering
import re


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    pass


@total_ordering
class Version:
    def __init__(self, s):
        if not isinstance(s, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*", s):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid version: {s!r}")
        self.original = s
        parts = tuple(int(part) for part in s.split("."))
        while parts and parts[-1] == 0:
            parts = parts[:-1]
        self.parts = parts

    def __str__(self):
        return self.original

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts == other.parts

    def __lt__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts < other.parts

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self.parts)


class Constraint:
    def __init__(self, name, clauses):
        self.name = name
        self.clauses = clauses

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        match = re.fullmatch(r"\s*([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s*(.*?)\s*", requirement)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
        name, suffix = match.groups()
        clauses = []
        if suffix:
            for clause in suffix.split(","):
                match = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*)\s*", clause)
                if not match:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
                op, version = match.groups()
                clauses.append((op, Version(version)))
        return cls(name, clauses)

    def allows(self, version):
        for op, target in self.clauses:
            if not {"==": version == target, "!=": version != target,
                    "<": version < target, "<=": version <= target,
                    ">": version > target, ">=": version >= target}[op]:
                return False
        return True


def resolve(roots, index):
    # Parse once: branches share immutable versions and dependency constraints.
    candidates = {
        name: sorted(((Version(raw), tuple(Constraint.parse(dep) for dep in deps))
                      for raw, deps in versions.items()),
                     key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
        for name, versions in index.items()
    }
    requirements = {}
    for root in roots:
        constraint = Constraint.parse(root)
        requirements.setdefault(constraint.name, []).append(constraint)

    names = sorted(set(index) | set(requirements))
    best = None
    best_key = None
    dead_end = None

    def score(versions):
        # Absence sorts below every version, including zero. This also supplies
        # a consistent ordering for solutions with different reachable packages.
        return tuple((1, versions[name].parts) if name in versions else (0, ())
                     for name in names)

    def search(chosen, constraints):
        nonlocal best, best_key, dead_end
        domains = {}
        for name, rules in constraints.items():
            domain = [item for item in candidates.get(name, ())
                      if all(rule.allows(item[0]) for rule in rules)
                      and (name not in chosen or item[0] == chosen[name])]
            if not domain:
                dead_end = name
                return
            domains[name] = domain

        # Every possible future dependency contributes an upper bound. Ignoring
        # its new constraints can only overestimate a branch's attainable score.
        potential = dict(domains)
        pending = list(potential)
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            for _, dependencies in potential[name]:
                for dep in dependencies:
                    if dep.name not in potential:
                        potential[dep.name] = candidates.get(dep.name, ())
                        pending.append(dep.name)
        upper = {name: domain[0][0] for name, domain in potential.items() if domain}
        if best_key is not None and score(upper) <= best_key:
            return

        unresolved = sorted(set(constraints) - set(chosen))
        if not unresolved:
            best = chosen.copy()
            best_key = score(best)
            return
        name = unresolved[0]
        for version, dependencies in domains[name]:
            next_constraints = {pkg: list(rules) for pkg, rules in constraints.items()}
            for dep in dependencies:
                next_constraints.setdefault(dep.name, []).append(dep)
            search({**chosen, name: version}, next_constraints)

    search({}, requirements)
    if best is None:
        raise ResolutionError(f"Cannot satisfy constraints for package {dead_end}")
    return {name: str(best[name]) for name in sorted(best)}
